about: TODAY'S deployed (V1) attested outputs: a Bytes<LEN> at one of THREE widths, with no kind byte. 0 — the EMPTY output, which queueAttestation0 takes and which EVERY failed or unviable verdict carries whatever the request asked for; 1 — the EVM bool, as a raw byte (any byte is accepted and everything but 0x01 routes to the failure branch: the 0x02 hazard); 32 — one big-endian ABI word, which is how V1 carries every uint256 the destination chain returns (the swap's amountIn, the supply's shares, the redeem's assets). There is NO failure sentinel: the superseded 5-byte 0xdeadbeef01 output has no successor, because the verdict and the output's width are signed into the attestation digest instead. That digest is Poseidon over FIELD elements — [HashDomain, requestId, blockHeight, outputKind, LEN, ..output] — so it has no byte preimage and no vector here.
